claim: Regular sessions convene every year on the second Monday of January
quote: Regular sessions of the legislature shall be held annually, commencing on the second Monday of January.

claim: Odd-year regular sessions run at most 105 consecutive days
quote: During each odd-numbered year, the regular session shall not be more than one hundred five consecutive days.

claim: Even-year regular sessions run at most 60 consecutive days
quote: During each even-numbered year, the regular session shall not be more than sixty consecutive days.

claim: Bills presented after adjournment become law unless the governor vetoes within 20 days, Sundays excepted
quote: it shall become a law unless the governor, within twenty days next after the adjournment, Sundays excepted, shall file such bill with his objections thereto

claim: Bills presented during session become law if not returned within five days, Sundays excepted
quote: If any bill shall not be returned by the governor within five days, Sundays excepted, after it shall be presented to him, it shall become a law without his signature

claim: Laws subject to referendum take effect 90 days after the session adjourns
quote: No act, law, or bill subject to referendum shall take effect until ninety days after the adjournment of the session at which it was enacted.

claim: Primaries for November general elections are held on the first Tuesday of August
quote: must be held on the first Tuesday of the preceding August

claim: A statewide general election is held every year on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November
quote: A statewide general election shall be held on the first Tuesday after the first Monday of November of each year.

claim: The odd-year statewide general election is limited mainly to city, town and district elections
quote: the statewide general election held in odd-numbered years shall be limited to (a) city, town, and district general elections

claim: A charter county may hold its county elections in the odd-year general election
quote: the election of county officers in any county governed by a charter containing provisions calling for general county elections at this time

claim: City, town and district general elections are held in November of odd-numbered years
quote: All city, town, and district general elections shall be held throughout the state of Washington on the first Tuesday following the first Monday in November in the odd-numbered years.

claim: Public utility districts, conservation districts and property-owner districts are outside the odd-year rule
quote: Public utility districts, conservation districts, or district elections at which the ownership of property within those districts is a prerequisite to voting

claim: The odd-year dates are mandatory and override other statutes
quote: the purpose of this section being to establish mandatory dates for holding elections

claim: County officers are elected every four years at the November election in a year counted from 1922, so in even years
quote: and every four years thereafter on the Tuesday next following the first Monday in November

claim: County officers serve four-year terms
quote: The term of office of all county and precinct officers shall be four years

claim: County commissioners serve four-year staggered terms, with one or two elected in each even-numbered year
quote: either one or two commissioners are elected at a general election held in each even-numbered year

claim: County offices are partisan except judicial offices and offices a county charter makes otherwise
quote: All county offices except (a) judicial offices and (b) those offices for which a county home rule charter provides otherwise.

claim: State offices, including the legislature, are partisan except judges and the superintendent of public instruction
quote: All state offices, including legislative, except (a) judicial offices and (b) the office of superintendent of public instruction

claim: A partisan office is one where the candidate may show a party preference on the ballot
quote: means a public office for which a candidate may indicate a political party preference on his or her declaration of candidacy

claim: All city, town and special purpose district offices are nonpartisan
quote: All city, town, and special purpose district elective offices shall be nonpartisan and the candidates therefor shall be nominated and elected as such.

claim: City and town primaries are nonpartisan
quote: All city and town primaries shall be nonpartisan.

claim: Partisan offices use a top-two primary
quote: the top two candidates will be certified as qualified to appear on the general election ballot

claim: A candidate may state a party preference, or none
quote: A candidate may choose to express no party preference.

claim: Party preference on the ballot is information only and limits nobody
quote: Any party preferences are shown for the information of voters only and may in no way limit the options available to voters.

claim: The ballot prints the preference as "Prefers ... Party" or "States No Party Preference"
quote: John Smith (Prefers ABC Party)

claim: A candidate who states no preference is shown as "States No Party Preference"
quote: (States No Party Preference)

claim: Voters never register by party
quote: Under no circumstances may an individual be required to affiliate with, join, adhere to, express faith in, or declare a preference for, a political party or organization upon registering to vote.

claim: No primary for a nonpartisan position with two or fewer candidates
quote: there are no more than two candidates filed for the position

claim: Park and recreation district and cemetery district commissioners have no primary
quote: No primary may be held for the office of commissioner of a park and recreation district or for the office of cemetery district commissioner.

claim: Only the top two from the primary appear in November, and only with at least 1 percent of the primary vote
quote: unless he or she receives at least one percent of the total votes cast for that office at the preceding primary

claim: The commissioner with the most votes is elected
quote: the person receiving the highest number of votes for the office of commissioner for the district in which he or she resides shall be declared duly elected from that district

claim: Every candidate files a declaration of candidacy, with a party preference line only for partisan offices
quote: A place for the candidate to state a party preference, if the office is a partisan office

claim: A candidate who cannot pay the filing fee may file a filing fee petition instead
quote: shall submit with the candidate's declaration of candidacy a filing fee petition

claim: Only voters registered within the office's jurisdiction may sign a filing fee petition
quote: The signatures shall be of voters registered to vote within the jurisdiction of the office for which the candidate is filing.

claim: Every active registered voter is mailed a ballot for every election
quote: shall automatically be issued a mail ballot for each general election, special election, or primary

claim: There are 39 counties, one boundary section each from Adams (36.04.010) to Yakima (36.04.390)
quote: Yakima county shall consist of the territory bounded as follows

claim: Each county has a board of three commissioners by default
quote: each board of county commissioners shall consist of three qualified electors

claim: Commissioners are nominated by district
quote: the qualified electors of each county commissioner district, and they only, shall nominate from among their own number

claim: Noncharter counties of 400,000 or more elect commissioners by district
quote: in any noncharter county with a population of four hundred thousand or more, county commissioners must be nominated and elected by the qualified electors of the commissioner district in which he or she resides

claim: Some noncharter counties may move to five commissioners by vote
quote: authorizing the board of commissioners to be increased to five members

claim: Five-member boards are nominated by district and elected countywide
quote: Each shall be elected by the voters of the entire county.

claim: Default elected county officers
quote: a county assessor, a county auditor, a county clerk, a county coroner, three county commissioners, a county prosecuting attorney, a county sheriff, and a county treasurer

claim: Counties under 40,000 may appoint rather than elect a coroner
quote: in each county with a population of less than forty thousand the county legislative authority may determine that no coroner shall be elected

claim: Any county may adopt a home rule charter, subject to the constitution and state law
quote: Any county may frame a "Home Rule" charter for its own government subject to the Constitution and laws of this state

claim: A county charter cannot change the election of the prosecuting attorney or superior court judges
quote: shall not affect the election of the prosecuting attorney, the county superintendent of schools, the judges of the superior court, and the justices of the peace

claim: The constitution permits combined city-county governments
quote: which authorizes the formation of combined city and county municipal corporations

claim: Township government law is no longer in the code: Title 45, Townships, survives only as a dispositions table
quote: COUNTY-WIDE DISORGANIZATION OF TOWNSHIPS

claim: King County executive, assessor, council and prosecuting attorney elections follow the law for nonpartisan county officers
quote: shall be conducted in accordance with general law governing the election of nonpartisan county officers

claim: King County executive and assessor are nonpartisan
quote: The county executive and county assessor shall be elected as nonpartisan offices by the voters of the county

claim: King County director of elections is an elected nonpartisan office
quote: The county director of elections shall be elected as a nonpartisan office by the voters of the county

claim: King County prosecuting attorney is nonpartisan
quote: The county prosecuting attorney shall be elected as a nonpartisan office by the voters of the county

claim: King County has nine council districts
quote: The county shall be divided into nine districts numbered one through nine

claim: King County moved its county elections to even-numbered years from 2026
quote: in even-numbered years commencing in 2026 and every four years thereafter

claim: First-class city: 10,000 or more at organization, with a charter
quote: A first-class city is a city with a population of ten thousand or more at the time of its organization or reorganization that has a charter adopted under Article XI, section 10, of the state Constitution.

claim: Second-class city: 1,500 or more at organization, no charter, not a code city
quote: A second-class city is a city with a population of fifteen hundred or more at the time of its organization or reorganization

claim: Town: under 1,500 at organization, not a code city
quote: A town has a population of less than fifteen hundred at the time of its organization and does not operate under Title 35A RCW.

claim: A noncharter code city can be any size
quote: A noncharter code city is one, regardless of population,

claim: A charter code city needs 10,000 inhabitants at organization
quote: A charter code city is one having at least ten thousand inhabitants at the time of its organization or reorganization

claim: Any city or town may become a noncharter code city
quote: Any incorporated city or town may become a noncharter code city

claim: A town that reaches 1,500 may, but need not, advance to second class
quote: A town which has at least fifteen hundred inhabitants may reorganize and advance its classification to become a second-class city

claim: A city of 10,000 or more may frame a charter, subject to state law
quote: Any city containing a population of ten thousand inhabitants, or more, shall be permitted to frame a charter for its own government, consistent with and subject to the Constitution and laws of this state

claim: City charters are controlled by general laws
quote: all charters thereof framed or adopted by authority of this Constitution shall be subject to and controlled by general laws

claim: Code city elections follow general election law
quote: Elections for code cities shall comply with general election law.

claim: Mayor-council code cities elect a mayor and council
quote: shall be vested in an elected mayor and an elected council

claim: Code city council: five members under 2,500 people, seven at 2,500 or more
quote: The council of a noncharter code city having less than twenty-five hundred inhabitants shall consist of five members; when there are twenty-five hundred or more inhabitants, the council shall consist of seven members.

claim: Code city mayor and council serve four-year terms
quote: The mayor and the councilmembers shall be elected for four-year terms of office

claim: Code city councils are at large unless a charter or ordinance creates wards
quote: unless provision is made by charter or ordinance for election by wards

claim: In council-manager code cities only the council is elected
quote: The councilmembers shall be the only elective officers of a code city electing to adopt the council-manager plan of government

claim: In council-manager code cities the council chair carries the title mayor
quote: The chair of the council shall have the title of mayor and shall preside at meetings of the council.

claim: Second-class cities elect a mayor, seven councilmembers, attorney, clerk and treasurer
quote: a city council of seven members, a city attorney, a clerk, a treasurer, all elective

claim: A second-class city may make its clerk, attorney and treasurer appointed
quote: the council may enact an ordinance providing for the appointment of the city clerk, city attorney, and treasurer by the mayor

claim: Second-class cities vote in odd years
quote: General municipal elections in second-class cities shall be held biennially in the odd-numbered years

claim: Second-class council position seven has a two-year term
quote: council position seven has a two-year term of office

claim: Towns elect a mayor, five councilmembers and a treasurer
quote: The government of a town shall be vested in a mayor and a council consisting of five members and a treasurer, all elective

claim: Town councilmembers serve four-year terms
quote: Councilmembers shall be elected for four year terms

claim: School boards have five directors
quote: the board of directors of every school district of the first class or school district of the second class shall consist of five members

claim: A district containing a city of 400,000 or more has seven directors
quote: which shall have a board of directors of seven members

claim: School directors serve four-year terms by default
quote: shall hold office for a term of four years

claim: School director races appear on the nonpartisan ballot
quote: shall appear separately on the nonpartisan ballot

claim: Some large first-class school districts may elect directors to six-year terms
quote: the directors to be elected may be elected for terms of six years

claim: Fire commissioners serve six-year terms
quote: The term of office of each subsequent commissioner shall be six years.

claim: Port commissioners serve four- or six-year terms
quote: In every port district the term of office of each port commissioner shall be four years

claim: Hospital district commissioners serve six-year terms
quote: The term of office of each successor shall be six years.

claim: Water-sewer district commissioners serve six-year terms
quote: the term of office of each district commissioner shall be six years

claim: Park and recreation districts have five commissioners elected in odd years without a primary
quote: Elections for park and recreation district commissioners shall be held biennially in conjunction with the general election in each odd-numbered year.

claim: PUD commissions have three or five members by district
quote: The powers of the public utility district shall be exercised through a commission consisting of three members in three commissioner districts, and five members in five commissioner districts.
